title: Knowledge check: Resources and Resource Identification

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly distinguishes REST from HTTP?
options: Any API that sends JSON is necessarily a strict REST implementation.
REST requires every service to use one particular programming language.
REST is an architectural style; HTTP is a protocol, and an HTTP JSON API does not automatically satisfy every REST constraint.
REST is a new HTTP method that replaces GET and POST.
questions.answer_key: REST is an architectural style; HTTP is a protocol, and an HTTP JSON API does not automatically satisfy every REST constraint.
questions.explanation: REST is an architectural style; HTTP is a protocol, and an HTTP JSON API does not automatically satisfy every REST constraint. This is especially relevant to “Resources and Resource Identification” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “Resources and Resource Identification”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Review the declared REST constraints and avoid claiming constraints that are not implemented.
Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
questions.answer_key: Review the declared REST constraints and avoid claiming constraints that are not implemented.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “Resources and Resource Identification”?
options: The design labels an HTTP JSON API as strict REST without considering the architectural constraints.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
questions.answer_key: The design labels an HTTP JSON API as strict REST without considering the architectural constraints.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
